_comment: WO-5 preparation only (owner-approved 2026-10-05): time ADR 0020's cell A before any cell runs,
and re-price the cell table from the measurement (WO-5 'Before the first cell'; ADR 0020 stop
rule 7). START NO CELL. Deviation from the brief's 'time one pass', approved by the coordinator:
one CPU pass of cell A was projected at about 23-24 h (ADR 0020's A(L,d,b) cost model scaled
from cell 0b's measured 0.297 s CPU step: 8.0x per example, about 2.2 s per step, 38,554
steps per full pass; ADR 0020's own projection was 27.1 h). So the first 2,000 optimizer steps
are timed on the full dataset and extrapolated by the step count. Every step has the same
shape (512 examples of 100-long left-padded windows, 1,024 negatives, a fixed catalog), so
the steady-state step time carries to the pass within a few percent. The owner can still ask
for the literal full pass. Steps 1-20 are excluded as warm-up. Data loading, the split, the
user-history build and the example-store build are timed separately from stepping; peak RSS is
the process's. CPU first (the one full-data run in flight, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 as every recorded
full-data SASRec run used), then mps on the same 2,000 steps: TIMING ONLY, NOT A RESULT OF
RECORD. No evaluation, no export, no MLflow run: the fit is interrupted after the last step.
Cell A per ADR 0020: hidden 128, 2 blocks, 4 heads, feed-forward 4x (512), dropout 0.2,
history 100, sampled softmax with 1,024 negatives, 512 examples per step, Adam 1e-3, seed 42,
objective of record. Early stopping is off for the timing (the probe carve is setup, not

timing.extrapolation: steady-state mean step seconds x steps per pass (ceil(examples / 512))
